what_its_for: Ethambutol is an antibiotic used to treat tuberculosis (TB), a serious infection that mainly affects the lungs. It is always used together with other TB medicines as part of a combination treatment plan. It works by stopping the TB bacteria from growing and spreading in your body.
how_to_take: Take ethambutol by mouth with or without food. If it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or a snack. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it at the same time every day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. Never skip doses or stop taking it early, even if you feel better, because the TB bacteria may come back stronger and harder to treat.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your weight and the type of TB being treated. A common adult dose is 15 to 25 mg per kilogram of body weight taken once daily. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor or pharmacist first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember that same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store ethambutol at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain aluminum (such as Maalox or Mylanta) within 4 hours of taking ethambutol, as they can reduce how well the medicine is absorbed. Avoid drinking alcohol, as it may increase the risk of side effects. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some may interact with ethambutol.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice any changes in your vision, such as blurry vision, trouble seeing colors (especially red and green), or any loss of vision — this is a serious side effect that needs immediate attention. Also contact your doctor if you experience numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, signs of liver problems (yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, nausea, or unusual tiredness), a skin rash, fever, chills, or any new or worsening symptoms.
when_it_works: TB treatment takes a long time — usually at least 6 months. You may start feeling better within a few weeks, but it is very important to keep taking all your TB medicines for the full length of time your doctor prescribes. Stopping early can allow the infection to return and become resistant to treatment.
special_populations: Children: Ethambutol can be used in children, but the dose is based on their weight. Vision testing may be harder in young children, so your doctor will monitor them carefully. Older adults: Use with caution, as kidney function may be reduced with age, which can increase the risk of side effects. Kidney problems: Your dose may need to be adjusted if you have kidney disease. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of this medicine may pass into breast milk; discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor.
